## cfoai
# cfo.ai MCP

You are connected to **cfo.ai** — an AI-native financial planning workspace. This MCP exposes Ari's public product tools for you to call directly. You can both **read** a company's financial model and **change** it: create and edit scenarios, pages, table blocks, Canvas blocks, formulas, variables, dimensions, and data ingestion.

Model-editing tools change the live model immediately and record reversible changes in its
changelog. Connections, access changes, and outbound actions have effects outside model undo. Build from saved data, research, supplied numbers, estimates, hypotheses, or invented
assumptions. Clearly label uncited inputs and their basis in the model and handoff. Create missing
model objects and editable inputs as part of the work. A missing source citation does not block modeling.

## Read the reference before you build

cfo.ai has its own modeling method, described under "How a table shows the model" below: how tables show variables, dimensions, and fields, how a reference reads from the cell it sits in, and how a table's rows and columns are built. `inspect_skills` owns the built-in and workspace skill catalog. Use its `list` block to find a skill and its `instructions` block to read it.

Read `build-model` before creating or changing model logic, variables, dimensions, or saved tables;
`build-visualizations` before adding a Canvas block; and `import-model` before rebuilding a model
from a workbook or export. Each manual contains its complete reference in `SKILL.md`.

Workspace skills hold company-specific playbooks. Read the relevant saved guidance before substantial work.

## Calling convention

- A multi-action tool selects one operation with the block named for that action; single-purpose tools use their fields directly. Supply only fields supported inside the selected block. An `inspect_*` tool reads saved product state; an `edit_*` tool changes it.
- `target` identifies an existing object where the operation needs one, including the destination of a new block. Creation fields describe the new object: use the selected operation's `name`, `title`, `source`, or other published fields. On an update, `name` gives the selected object's new name.
- Supply `org_id` when selecting a workspace by ID or slug. If you belong to exactly one workspace, the server selects it automatically. Use `list_orgs` when the correct workspace is unclear.
- Tools accept an optional `_context` object — `{ layerId, pageId, timeZone, utcOffset }` — that mirrors the in-app editing context. Supply `layerId` for the active scenario, `pageId` for the current page, and `timeZone` or `utcOffset` when relative dates matter. Identify existing objects by readable names or references returned by an inspection.
- Model object selectors accept names, returned `Name#hex` disambiguators, or IDs unless the field states a narrower contract. A returned `Name#a1b` carries a prefix of the object's identity, at least three hex digits and unique among every object of its kind when the result was written; later creates can lengthen it, so a reference from an older result resolves while it stays unique, and a fresh inspection carries the current spelling. Ambiguous or unknown names return candidates when available. Each tool defines singular or plural targets, omitted/empty/null input behavior, and scenario defaults.
- Reuse pagination cursors unchanged with the same tool, action, target, filters, and snapshot. Each cursor field names the returned value to use and any special empty-string behavior.
- A saved table is created or reshaped with its complete visible `rows` and `columns`. A dimension path may use a bounded member `filter`, an ancestor `when` condition, or independent sibling `branches`. Inspection returns the same saved shape under `layout.rows` and `layout.columns`. Updates use `row_updates`, `column_updates`, and `cell_updates`. An `add_dimension_items` entry places a planned member `under` an existing inspected parent.
- A Canvas block reads model values through named `datasets`. Each dataset declares the same visible sh… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## crustdata
People and organisations: 800M+ profiles, 200M+ companies. Employment history with dates, titles and seniority, education, skills, location, headcount over time, funding, technologies, job postings, social posts, work emails and phone numbers. Filter, combine, count and sort across any of it — people who studied at one place and now work at another, everyone hired into a role since a date, faculty at an institution, alumni of a company, who is hiring, who left and where they went, how many match. Live web search and page fetch too.

When you cannot serve a Crustdata ask, or serve it wrong, because of Crustdata itself — missing or wrong data, no filter or field for the ask (even when you worked around it), a server error that keeps failing, a schema or error message that misled you — report it with the `feedback` tool, once per problem, then keep working. Not for plan gates (403), credits (402), rate limits, the user's own mistakes, or asks outside Crustdata.

Crustdata MCP — Code Mode over the Crustdata API. You drive it by writing a plain-JavaScript script (no type annotations — author against the TypeScript-typed tool surface from get_schema) for execute({ code }); the only I/O is `const r = await callTool(name, params)`.

Core rules (they hold for every script):
- **Write runnable JavaScript — NO type syntax.** The script executes as plain JS in a V8 isolate; the TypeScript types are the tool *surface* you read from `get_schema`, not something you write in the body. A type annotation in the code — `: Type`, `as`, `interface`/`type`/`enum`, or generics `<T>` — is a parse error that fails the WHOLE run (zero spend, before any tool call). Author against the types; emit only the JS.
- **One I/O primitive:** `const r = await callTool(name, params)` → `{ ok: true, data, credits_used? } | { ok: false, status, errorType, message }`. `credits_used` is the server's exact charge for that call (data-API tools only; `0` = free/preview, and an async batch SUBMIT — billed at job completion, not on submit) — sum it to track spend mid-run. `upstream_request_id` is the API's own id for that call, present on success and failure alike when the response carried one — quote it when reporting a failed or disputed charge, it is the join key to the API's own record. A failure that stopped for want of credits also carries `top_up_url`, and the run's result then carries `out_of_credits` with the sentence to relay; put that link in your reply exactly as written, since the person who can buy credits is the one reading it. A `permission_error` because the account hasn't completed its first purchase carries `paywall_url` instead — relay that link exactly as written too.
- **await ONLY `callTool`, `sleep`, `paginate`, and `parallelMap`** — the query-builder and result-shaper helpers are synchronous; awaiting one is a harmless no-op (`await` on a non-promise returns it unchanged), just needless — so don't.
- **Fan out INDEPENDENT work — don't await in a loop.** When you have N independent calls (enrich/lookup a list, per-entity sub-queries, several unrelated searches), run them at once with `await parallelMap(items, fn)` instead of a `for … await` loop — far faster and it keeps a big bulk run under the wall-clock (same credits either way). BATCH first (`chunk` to the per-call cap, e.g. 25 for enrich), then `parallelMap` the batches. NEVER parallelize: cursor pagination (use `paginate` — each page needs the prior cursor), dependent steps (`search → enrich`: keep the pipeline sequential, parallelize only WITHIN a stage), or accumulate-then-decide / early-exit (parallel can't stop early → pays for all N).
- **Always branch on `r.ok`** — a failed call does NOT abort the script, so an unchecked failure silently proceeds on empty data and looks like "no results". Use `unwrap(await callTool(...))` when a step must succeed; `execute` also returns a `tool_errors` list, so empty ≠ failed stays visible.
- **Run the question you were asked.** The query you execute must encode the user's intent at the same precision, scope, set-logic, and tense — silently swappin… [truncated]

## plugin:small-business:google-drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Starting a New Business
Users who are still shaping a business can work on it here before they have a store. None of these tools needs one.
- Naming: generate-business-names suggests business names from a short description of what the user sells, who it is for, or the feeling they want.
- Domains: generate-domain-names checks whether a name or domain idea is available and what it costs to register, and suggests available alternatives.
When the user settles on a name, offer to check domains for it.
Never present a domain as available unless generate-domain-names checked it; a domain you suggest yourself may already be taken.
Follow the user's lead rather than walking them through every step.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
For store data without a dedicated built-in tool, use the read-only GraphQL Workflow below. For writes without a dedicated tool, discover the operation with graphql_schema, validate it with validate_graphql_codeblocks, then execute it with graphql_mutation.

Decision logic:
1. Prefer a built-in tool when it matches the request.
2. Otherwise, start at graphql_schema with operation 'query' to discover the exact query field rather than guessing.

## GraphQL Workflow
Build a read-only GraphQL query in this order:
1. graphql_schema with operation 'query': list the top-level query names or search them, then inspect the exact field_name to learn its arguments and return type.
2. graphql_schema with operation 'schema' and type_name: inspect each named argument and return type needed to select fields or construct variables. Follow named nested input types with further calls.
3. Construct the query, then call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before execution. Do NOT skip validation.
4. graphql_query: execute the read-only query only after validation passes. setup-mcp also validates it against the pinned Admin schema before sending it to Admin. search_docs_chunks can supplement discovery with examples but cannot replace the schema tools.

For mutation schema discovery, use graphql_schema with operation 'mutation' to list or search mutation names, then inspect an exact field_name. Follow its argument and return types with operation 'schema' and type_name. Discovery does not execute mutations. After constructing a mutation, call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before graphql_mutation.

## Shop Resolution
The shop is automatically resolved from the authenticated token — you do not need to ask the user which store to use.
Use get-shop-info when you need store context (name, plan, currency, timezone) to tailor your advice.
Only ask the user to clarify which shop to use if a tool call fails with a shop resolution error or if the user has explicitly mentioned a different store.

## Live Data Rules
When the user references their store data, you MUST call the appropriate tool to fetch live data. This includes built-in tools AND graphql_query/graphql_mutation when no built-in … [truncated]

7	| `bdd1f6f1` latency | `gemini-3.7-flash` calls hit `504 Deadline expired` at about 87 s; cause "not established" (0.65) | Traces `050dc8b8...` and `08177d77...`: exactly one Gemini call errored at 87.6 s and 87.7 s, the retry succeeded, and the stall was about 40% of a 224-241 s run. The client timeout was 90 s for every call; normal text calls take 3-18 s | **Confirmed** (the card's own recommended step was "inspect the client timeout") | [HR-005](../hardening/HR-005.md): 40 s timeout for text and vision, images keep 90 s |
8	| `ebcff17a` safety false positive | `verify:story_safe_text` flags benign "hurts" as critical and halts the workflow (0.70) | "hurt", "hurts", "fight" were on the blocklist and any hit was `critical`. But no run in the ledger ended `stopped`, and the "workflow halt (returning null)" is a misreading: the workflow span's output is always null | **Partly confirmed**: the false positive is real, the halt is not | [HR-004](../hardening/HR-004.md): mild terms ask for a rewrite; severe terms stay critical |
9	| `67e5d3bd` PII filter | An over-aggressive PII/NER filter in our workflow replaces "honest", "forest" and hero names with `<PERSON>`/`<LOCATION>`, causing repair loops (0.77) | `grep` finds no `<PERSON>` in our code (our only placeholder is `[personal details]`, used for personal data found in a drawing). The placeholders are neatlogs's own server-side redaction of trace text (we set `pii_enabled` with PERSON, LOCATION and others). The story logic sees real text. `character_named_in_scene` never failed in B1; the 254 B1 reading-level failures and the other repairs have nothing to do with names | **Not confirmed**: it read redacted trace text as if it were the app's behaviour | Nothing changed in the app. Trade-off noted: redaction protects against names or places in drawings reaching traces, and makes traces (and neatlogs's own AI) harder to read |
10	
11	Reading the three together: the platform found one real latency problem and one real (if smaller than claimed) false positive from traces alone, and misdiagnosed a third because redaction hid the real text. == HR-001
# HR-001: reading level broke on almost every page (prompt p1 to p2)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `age_reading_level` ("Sentences are short and the words are easy for this age"; deterministic check, limit 14 words per sentence at age 6).

## Trigger

The first full run and the first baseline sweep (`sweep-1-p1`) both showed `age_reading_level` failing on the first pass for nearly every page: the writer produced 15 to 22 word sentences against a 14 word limit. In sweep 1 it was the most common broken promis

- Trace of one affected story (before): `264208295ada9b28a96d2e29b32fb41c` (bunny, sharing, B1, seed 1; 7 reading-level violations, 7 repairs, 358.6 s). Export: `evidence/traces/20261010-1508-IST-sweep1-p1-bunny-sharing-B1-7-reading-level-repairs.json`.

## Diagnosis

== HR-002
# HR-002: gated stories took too long (pipelined review)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Not a broken promise but a cost of verifying: the gate made B1 stories slower than the ungated arm.

## Trigger

In `sweep-1-p1` a gated story (B1) took 246.8 s on average against 180.5 s for the ungated baseline (B0), about 1.37 times as long, and a child would wait for the whole of it. Every page was written, then reviewed by the slow independent judge (K2), then repai

- Trace (before the change): `264208295ada9b28a96d2e29b32fb41c` (bunny, sharing, B1, seed 1; 358.6 s). Export: `evidence/traces/20261010-1508-IST-sweep1-p1-bunny-sharing-B1-7-reading-level-repairs.json`.

## Diagnosis

== HR-003
# HR-003: the page writer kept overshooting the reading limit (prompt p2 to p3)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `age_reading_level` (limit 14 words per sentence at age 6). Follows [HR-001](HR-001.md), whose "what is still wrong" section named this.

## Trigger

After HR-001 the page-by-page writer in B1 was still over the limit on 22 of 224 first-pass pages (9.8%) in `sweep-2-p2`, against 4 of 224 (1.8%) for the one-call baseline. In the trace of one failing page (`a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f`, scene 7) the page

## Diagnosis

Hypothesis, written before the change: stating the limit made it the writer's target, and a model aiming at 14 overshoots by a word about one time in ten. A target two words under the limit should leave room. For the compound word: the long-word check should s

== HR-005
# HR-005: one Gemini call stalled for 87 s per trace (neatlogs triage card): tried a 40 s timeout, not kept

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Not a broken promise but latency: time lost to a model call that never answered.

## Trigger

neatlogs's automatic triage opened card `bdd1f6f1` ("Investigate Gemini 3.7 Flash 504 Timeout", severity high, confidence 0.65, "root cause not established"). Traces `050dc8b85289002f084c67e8cfc23a42` and `08177d773d0e88d8b26febc22898ba03`: exactly one `gemini

## Diagnosis

The card's own first step was "check the configured timeout". Confirmed: every Gemini call used `request_timeout_s = 90`, while normal text and vision calls take 3-18 s. Hypothesis: a 40 s timeout for text and vision calls (images keep 90 s) would turn an 87 s

# HR-006: the image model painted words into a child's picture

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Found by looking at the frames of the first story video, not by a check: no promise covered it.

## Trigger

In the first illustrated story (`story-video-1`, trace `0fd459e70b5165e1455980c72c77f66d`, 8 pictures, 8 narration clips, cost estimate $0.358) the last page's picture had its caption painted into it: "The sun sets over the hill." and "Zuzu wiggles h..." (cut

# HR-007: a per-minute quota error ended a run (quota errors back off longer)

Date: 11 Oct 2026. Found by `sweep-7-quiz`, not by a check.

Two of the first 28 jobs in `sweep-7-quiz` (both `christmas-tree-digital`, seed 1, lessons sharing and honesty) ended with `outcome: error` at the **first model call** (28 and 33 seconds in): `ClientError: 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` from Vertex. Traces `65e993be9

## Trigger

## Diagnosis

# HR-004: a lesson saying "hurts trust" was a critical safety hit (neatlogs triage card)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `story_safe_text` (deterministic word lists on everything a child will read).

## Trigger

neatlogs's automatic triage opened card `ebcff17a` ("Overly restrictive deterministic blocklist in `verify:story_safe_text`", severity critical, confidence 0.70): a page whose feedback said "Pretending keeps a secret that hurts trust." was judged `critical` because of the word "hurts". Trace `26fbc879cddba411dc327286643276c3`; raw card in `evidence/neatlogs/20261010-1757-IST-triage-cards.json`; the review of all three cards is in [TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md).

## Diagnosis

Checked against our code and the ledger, not taken on trust:

- Confirmed: `hurt`, `hurts`, `fight`, `fights`, `fighting`, `fought` were in `HARM_TERMS`, and any hit made the verdict `critical`, which the pipeline treats as "regenerate once, then stop" rather than "repair".
- Not confirmed: the card says the workflow halted ("`create-storybook` returning `null`"). A workflow span's output is always `null`, and no run in the ledger ended `stopped` (0 of 156 story runs), so no story actually stopped; the cost of a false hit was a page regenerated.
- A product that teaches honesty and sharing will use "hurts" and "fight" gently ("friends do not fight", "a secret that hurts trust"). A hard stop on those words is the wrong severity; a rewrite is the right one, which is what the module's own comment says ("a false alarm costs one repair").

## Change

- Commit `748ce42` (Entire checkpoint `01M4JW5XY38RXXWY9MMWWYDP7Z`): severe terms (kill, gun, knife, blood, weapon, bomb, death, punch, attack, gore, suicide and similar) stay `critical`; mild terms (hurt, hurts, fight, fights, fighting, fought) and unkind labels now give an ordinary `violation`, which means the page is rewritten. Instruction-steering text and personal data stay `critical`.
- Regression test: `test_a_lesson_can_say_hurts_without_stopping_the_story` uses the card's own sentence ("hurts" is a violation), plus a knife (critical) and a plain sentence (pass).

## Before and after

The effect on our sweeps is small and we do not claim more: across 99 B1 jobs only 1 page was ever a `critical` story_safe_text hit (sweep 1; sweep 5 has 1 more of unknown cause), and no run stopped. The word lists run on text we do not store per page, so a replay of old pages through the new rule is not possible; the behaviour is pinned by the test instead. Severe-term behaviour is unchanged by construction. What changed is what a gentle lesson costs: a rewrite instead of a regeneration.

## Regression fixture

`tests/test_oath.py::test_a_lesson_can_say_hurts_without_stopping_the_story`.

import json, re, collections, os
R = r"D:\storybound\evidence\neatlogs\review-2"
cs = json.loads(open(os.path.join(R, "error_cause_search.json"), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read())
pool = json.load(open(os.path.join(R, "trace_pool.json")))
det = {}
for f in ("trace_detail.json", "trace_detail_err.json"):
    p = os.path.join(R, f)
    if os.path.exists(p):
        det.update({k: v for k, v in json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8")).items() if "head" in v})
PATS = [
    ("504 deadline (Gemini text)", r"ServerError 504|Deadline expired"),
    ("429 quota (image)", r"429[^a-z]{0,20}RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.{0,80}check quota"),
    ("429 quota (text)", r"429.{0,40}Resource exhausted\. Please try again"),
    ("429 quota", r"ClientError 429|RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"),
    ("503 K2 gateway", r"InternalServerError.{0,30}503|gateway could not complete"),
    ("499 cancelled", r"499 CANCELLED|operation was cancelled"),
    ("parse error (no JSON)", r"ParseError"),
    ("page JSON missing field", r"missing 'image_prompt'"),
    ("validation (make-video spec)", r"ValidationError"),
]
causes = collections.defaultdict(set)
for k, v in cs.items():
    for tid, x in v.items():
        txt = " ".join(s[1] for s in x["snips"])
        for name, pat in PATS:
            if re.search(pat, txt):
                causes[tid].add(name)
errs = {t: v for t, v in pool.items() if v["status"] == "error"}
print("pool errors", len(errs), "with cause", sum(1 for t in errs if t in causes))
tally = collections.Counter()
rows = []
for tid, v in sorted(errs.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]["created_at"]):
    c = causes.get(tid, set())
    dd = det.get(tid)
    note = ""
    if dd:
        bn = collections.Counter(b["name"] for b in dd["bad"])
        note = dict(bn)
    for x in (c or {"UNCLASSIFIED"}):
        tally[x] += 1
    rows.append((tid[:12], v["created_at"][5:16], round((v["duration_ms"] or 0) / 1000), v["errored_span_count"], sorted(c), note))
for r in rows: print(r)
print(tally)
json.dump({t[:12]: sorted(causes.get(t, [])) for t in errs}, open(os.path.join(R, "error_causes.json"), "w"), indent=1)

# HR-005: one Gemini call stalled for 87 s per trace (neatlogs triage card): tried a 40 s timeout, not kept

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Not a broken promise but latency: time lost to a model call that never answered.

## Trigger

neatlogs's automatic triage opened card `bdd1f6f1` ("Investigate Gemini 3.7 Flash 504 Timeout", severity high, confidence 0.65, "root cause not established"). Traces `050dc8b85289002f084c67e8cfc23a42` and `08177d773d0e88d8b26febc22898ba03`: exactly one `gemini-3.7-flash` call per trace ended in error after 87.6 s and 87.7 s, the retry succeeded, and the stall was about 40% of a 224-241 s run. Raw card: `evidence/neatlogs/20261010-1757-IST-triage-cards.json`; [TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md).

## Diagnosis

The card's own first step was "check the configured timeout". Confirmed: every Gemini call used `request_timeout_s = 90`, while normal text and vision calls take 3-18 s. Hypothesis: a 40 s timeout for text and vision calls (images keep 90 s) would turn an 87 s stall into a 40 s one, because the retry already succeeds.

## Change and test

- Commit `ed2a5f8` (Entire checkpoint `01M4JW5VCR4C3HDMCZPFVGQ2K4`): `text_timeout_s = 40`, with an environment override `STORYBOUND_TEXT_TIMEOUT_S` so it could be tested.
- Test: the same 14 jobs (seed 1, B1, 7 drawings x 2 lessons) with 40 s (`sweep-5-hr45`) and straight afterwards with 90 s (`sweep-6-t90`). Calls that errored for 30 s or more were read from the neatlogs traces.

## Before and after

Before = the 90 s default (sweep 6, the control); after = the 40 s change (sweep 5). The change made things no better:

| | 40 s (sweep 5) | 90 s (sweep 6) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean / median / max seconds per story | 203.7 / 163.4 / 397.3 | 114.9 / 108.7 / 252.6 |
| Average successful Gemini call | 9.0 s | 4.2 s |
| Calls that errored for 30 s or more | 12 (all about 37 s, in 8 of 14 traces) | 0 |

## Result

**Not supported, so the default is back to 90 s** (this commit). With the shorter timeout 12 calls were killed at about 37 s and the stories were slower; with 90 s no call stalled at all. Two readings fit and we cannot separate them: the provider was slow during sweep 5 (the average successful call was twice as slow) and the 40 s limit killed calls that would have finished, or hangs only appear at some times. Sweep 4 (90 s, earlier) also had no stalls, so the 87 s hangs in the triage traces were not reproduced in any of the 42 jobs we ran afterwards. Without a reproduction there is no evidence the change helps, and some that it can hurt, so we do not keep it. If hangs return, the better fix 

What the card was right about: the stalls are real and the timeout was the place to look. What it did not show: that shortening the timeout is safe.

Sample sizes are 14 jobs per arm and outputs are sampled; the cost estimates and the provider's state at the time are not controlled.

## Regression fixture

None: nothing was kept. The override `STORYBOUND_TEXT_TIMEOUT_S` stays so the experiment can be repeated.

# neatlogs incident review (window 10 Oct 06:00 UTC to 11 Oct 08:00 UTC)

Read on 11 Oct 2026 from the neatlogs MCP (project "Mohammad's project", free tier). Raw files are in `evidence/neatlogs/review-2/`. Trace ids are the first 12 characters. This review adds to `evidence/neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md`; the three open triage cards are the same three and were not redone.

## What could and could not be read

- 79 of the 110 error traces were pulled (72%) and sorted by cause. 68 of them have full span detail. The rest are in the pool file only.
- `get_trace_context` does not return the error text of an errored span (status ERROR, empty output). The cause was read from `search_traces` snippets instead. For 15 error traces no error text exists in any indexed field, so their cause is a guess and is marked as one.
- The MCP rejects field projection and span filters ("not_enabled"), rejects broad queries ("Service Unavailable") and caps sessions (HTTP 429, wait about 80 s). Counts below come from narrower queries.
- The `waste` analytics view returns no rows. Nothing in it could be read.
- Sessions: `session_id` equals the trace id in every trace seen, so the sessions view has nothing to group.

## Fix now

1. **Two detections have never fired and are probably broken** ("Quiz question failed a promise", "Picture has words painted in"). Both ran a backfill over 1,299 traces with 0 flagged. After they were created at 03:12 UTC the ledger shows 24 quiz-question repairs in 20 runs (for example `5421ee090126`, `e3fc473c2ccd`, `b674a7508efd`). The saved patterns are `quiz_(...).{0,400}(violation|critical|verification_error)` and `image_no_text.{0,400}violation`. They run at "trace" level, while the verdict text sits in GUARDRAIL spans as `Commitment: quiz_x\nScope: ...\nStatus: violation` (several lines). Likely cause (a hypothesis): `.` does not cross line breaks, and the trace-level text is empty (the workflow output is always null, see HR-004). The working "Oath violation" rule uses `Status: violation` on `span_type GUARDRAIL`. Action: in the neatlogs dashboard set both to run on GUARDRAIL spans and use `Commitment: quiz_\w+[\s\S]{0,300}Status: (violation|critical|verification_error)` (and the same shape for `image_no_text`). Test by checking that the backfill flags the 20 quiz runs above. Two of the six alert rules depend on these two detections, so both are silent today.
2. **No alert can reach anyone.** Every rule read back has `channelMask` email false, slack false, webhookCount 0 (files `20261011-write-config-results.json`, `...-more-alerts-results.json`). They show in the dashboard only. Action: add one email or webhook channel to at least "Critical safety stop".
3. **About 85% of the traces are one-span orphans, which makes the headline numbers misleading.** In two 10-minute samples (10 Oct 12:30 and 11 Oct 07:10) the traces that mention the K2 judge were 36 orphans to 6 story traces, and 82 orphans to 13 story traces. An orphan has an empty workflow name, the model name as its root span and 1 span lasting 2 to 11 s. 1,832 of the 2,095 traces mention K2. That is why p50 is 5.3 s while a story takes about 160 s, and why the 5.25% error rate and the 2,095 count do not describe stories. Cause not found: `src/storybound/oath/engine.py:189` and `pipeline.py:236,505,611` already copy `contextvars`, so the neatlogs span parent is probably not carried by that copy (hypothesis). Action: run one story and count root traces; fix the judge call so it joins the story trace; until then filter dashboards and alerts to workflow `create-storybook` with more than 10 spans. Smaller version of the same problem: standalone probe and eval calls are also traced alone (`84672c2c44e2` smoke test, `d705e66e2d99` K2 call, `1d57b0016612` judge-bias run); set `environment` (it is null on every trace) to `eval` or `test` for them in `src/storybound/tracing.py` or the app entry point.
4. **The 87 s Gemini stall (HR-005) is back and is the main latency cause.** HR-005 reverted to a 90 s timeout because the 42 later jobs showed no stall. On 11 Oct between 06:55 and 07:16 UTC 13 error traces had one `gemini-3.7-flash` call that ended at about 87 s with 504 "Deadline expired" (for example `6c8c28dda3c9`, `1092b1bbc158`, `d0bb16b76ed0`, `55bb3418fe6f`, `8e2a6a444965`). All shipped (retry worked). Stalls come in bursts: 9 traces on 10 Oct 07:58 to 09:47, 8 at 37 s during the 40 s experiment (12:22 to 12:28), 1 at 14:20, none from 12:49 to 14:19 except that one, then the 13 above. That pattern fits the provider being slow for some minutes, not our timeout. Action: reopen HR-005 and run the hedged retry its own text proposes (start a second call after about 15 s and take the first answer), measured on the 11 Oct burst.
5. **429 on text is fixed; 429 on pictures is not.** Since HR-007 (commit `3a89004`, 03:13 UTC on 11 Oct) 8 traces had a text 429 and all 8 shipped; before it 2 sweep-7 jobs ended in `error`. Pictures are different: 8 traces had image 429s with 6 to 48 failed spans each (`c9a78b746d47` 48 failed spans, 402 s; `aeea65c6b2cd` 31; `bcbaab155d9b` 32; `0fd459e70b51` 27), and `illustrate` failed 17 of 66 calls. The app falls back to text-only pages, so no child sees an error, but a story spends 3 to 5 minutes retrying (`node.media` 172 to 307 s). Action: after two image 429s in one story, stop painting for that story (the `auto` policy already stops after two failures; check it applies to the `full` and `half` policies too).
6. **Error spans without any error text (15 traces).** Gemini failures of 0.6 to 1.1 s (for example `182e4ea264be`, `9ac60464c282`, `33a9c06a4b76`, `57233238e74c`, `a32498d66523` all at 10 Oct 07:58 to 08:48 when three arms ran at once, and `21f5547097cb`, `2776b05792e0`, `83ec4cf94685` at 12:16 to 12:49) show ERROR but no message. Probably quota bursts, but unproven. Action: record exception type and message on every ERROR span in the model client wrapper.
7. **Three triage cards are still open** (`bdd1f6f1`, `ebcff17a`, `67e5d3bd`). Mark them resolved or archived in the dashboard with a link to `TRIAGE-REVIEW.md` (the CLI cannot write them). Evidence: `triage_open.json`.

## Watch

- **Parse errors persist.** 4 traces (`ac528975dda1` missing `image_prompt`; `e46e796a4a9e`, `06dac7f3455f` and `148a4920b0e0` "no JSON found" with the page text cut off at about 120 characters in the message). All but the first two on 10 Oct shipped after a retry; `148a4920b0e0` (11 Oct 06:58) and a second one, `e8a7ceeb2621`, still happened later, so the writer returns broken JSON in about 1 story in 20. Not seen by children. Check whether the writer output is cut (limit 900 tokens in `agents/writer.py:97,145`) before changing anything.
- **Image cost is invisible in neatlogs.** For text-only stories neatlogs measures 28% more than the ledger estimate (133 matched traces: estimate 2.03 USD, measured 2.61 USD, median ratio 0.79). For stories with pictures it sees 11 to 18% of the cost: `0fd459e70b51` $0.0411 measured against $0.358 estimated; `a7dd9ae1b832` $0.0382 against $0.356; `94db23729dac` $0.0344 against $0.191. The cfo.ai change (275839) is labelled text and verification, which is correct; do not quote a neatlogs figure as the cost of an illustrated story. Window total 4.59 USD is text only.
- **The `make-video` traces** (10 traces, 4 to 8 minutes, 3 of the 4 slowest). In `1cf9255c913b` (532 s) the child spans add up to about 170 s (`narrate_scenes` 169 s); the other 360 s sit in no child span (probably rendering; not verified). One failed: `49953358144a` (11 Oct 11:56 IST first preview, "five" not a number in the scene spec, 12 s; fixed since, later previews have no error).
- **Detections by day** (UTC; hourly files in `detection_trends.json`):

  | Detection | 10 Oct | 11 Oct (to 07:22) | Note |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Oath violation | 585 | 24 | busiest hour 08:00 with 378 (three arms in parallel) |
  | Execution Failed | 298 | 14 | 111 in the 14:00 hour (image 429 runs) |

  | Critical safety stop | 13 | 0 (3 more at 07:07 to 07:13) | see below |
  | Expensive LLM Call (over $1) | 0 | 0 | cannot fire at these prices |

  Counts follow the number of runs per hour, so they do not show effect by themselves. Per story, from the ledger (B1 violations found per run): p1 8.5, then p2 (HR-001, commit 13:40 IST) 1.8, p3 (HR-003, 17:46 IST) 0.8, then rising to 1.6 to 3.1 as new promises and harder holdout drawings were added. Ungated B0: 7.3 then 3.5. HR-001 and HR-003 are visible in the per-story numbers; neatlogs hourly counts alone could not show them.
- **Oath hits per story are normally 1 to 3.** About 9.7% of B1 runs end `shipped_with_notes` (18 of 185). That share, not the first-pass hit count, is what to watch.
- **`Execution Failed` is not "the story failed".** 58 of the 62 error traces matched to the ledger shipped (45 shipped, 13 shipped with notes); 4 ended `error`. A trace is "error" when any span errored, even if the retry worked.
- **`ignore all` is still a critical term.** `06a2527e2d27` (benign christmas tree, 10 Oct 08:57) stopped on "ignore all" in a story. HR-004 kept steering phrases critical on purpose; check that a phrase like "ignore all the noise" is not flagged in a benign story.

## Ignore, expected

- **The 13 Critical safety stop traces** (window to 07:03 UTC on 11 Oct; the 3 later ones are the Haiku ablation below):

  | Trace | When (UTC) | What fired | Verdict |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `b8839d3c5c23`, `9226e2a194ba` | 10 Oct 07:49 | `evil-cat-knife-blood.png` refused (blood, weapon) in safety-eval and eval-2 | intended |
  | `2f7c60378c19` | 07:34 | 2-span test of the word "kill" | deliberate test |
  | `391a1ea14192` | 12:28 | `no_drawing_text_obedience`: "ignore" from the injection fixture appeared in the story; 1 repair, shipped | intended catch |
  | `196d160d19dd`, `94db23729dac`, `f43aac0962c1`, `11a2900d813d`, `76c35d5c7534`, `257acf701def`, `26fbc879cddb`, `a534baeb9d47` | 07:40 to 09:29 | `story_safe_text` on "fighting", "hurt", "hurts" in benign stories (rhinoceros, bunny, rabbit, mickey, injection fixtures) | false positives, all before HR-004 (commit 17:51 IST = 12:21 UTC) |
  | `06a2527e2d27` | 08:57 | "ignore all" in a benign christmas-tree story | false positive (still possible) |

  So 9 of 13 were false positives on benign text and 4 were intended. None of the 9 stopped a story (the ledger has no `stopped` outcome; the page was rewritten). After HR-004 there is no benign "hurt" stop in the window. The late 3 (`9a5f898abbec` 07:07, `c10ef4def317` 07:08, `4d8aca06c1a5` 07:13 on 11 Oct) come from the Claude Haiku screening ablation (`evidence/runs/20261011-1237-IST-safety-eval-haiku.json`): 1 is the intended unsafe fixture, 2 are Haiku refusing the benign-text fixtures `mild-insults-text` (hate_symbol) and `fish-kill-fish-caption` (violence). Not the production path.
- **Gemini 504 and 429 recovered by retry** (see Fix now 4 and 5): 58 of 62 matched error traces shipped.
- **Probe traces**: 9 error traces of 1 to 2 spans under 1.5 s are tests and probes (`84672c2c44e2`, `d705e66e2d99`, `9377b4373cb2`, `722715f50e8a`, `a1dc773730c7`, `d4244a031bd9`, `a399ec1dbdd8`, `5ee359c6569e`, `2de7e25d8acd`).

# neatlogs incident review (window 10 Oct 06:00 UTC to 11 Oct 08:00 UTC)

Read on 11 Oct 2026 from the neatlogs MCP (project "Mohammad's project", free tier). Raw files are in `evidence/neatlogs/review-2/`. Trace ids are the first 12 characters. This review adds to `evidence/neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md`; the three open triage cards are the same three and were not redone.

## What could and could not be read

- 79 of the 110 error traces were pulled (72%) and sorted by cause. 68 of them have full span detail. The rest are in the pool file only.
- `get_trace_context` does not return the error text of an errored span (status ERROR, empty output). The cause was read from `search_traces` snippets instead. For 15 error traces no error text exists in any indexed field, so their cause is a guess and is marked as one.
- The MCP rejects field projection and span filters ("not_enabled"), rejects broad queries ("Service Unavailable") and caps sessions (HTTP 429, wait about 80 s). Counts below come from narrower queries.
- The `waste` analytics view returns no rows. Nothing in it could be read.
- Sessions: `session_id` equals the trace id in every trace seen, so the sessions view has nothing to group.

## Fix now

1. **Two detections have never fired and are probably broken** ("Quiz question failed a promise", "Picture has words painted in"). Both ran a backfill over 1,299 traces with 0 flagged. After they were created at 03:12 UTC the ledger shows 24 quiz-question repairs in 20 runs (for example `5421ee090126`, `e3fc473c2ccd`, `b674a7508efd`). The saved patterns are `quiz_(...).{0,400}(violation|critical|verification_error)` and `image_no_text.{0,400}violation`. They run at "trace" level, while the verdict text sits in GUARDRAIL spans as `Commitment: quiz_x\nScope: ...\nStatus: violation` (several lines). Likely cause (a hypothesis): `.` does not cross line breaks, and the trace-level text is empty (the workflow output is always null, see HR-004). The working "Oath violation" rule uses `Status: violation` on `span_type GUARDRAIL`. Action: in the neatlogs dashboard set both to run on GUARDRAIL spans and use `Commitment: quiz_\w+[\s\S]{0,300}Status: (violation|critical|verification_error)` (and the same shape for `image_no_text`). Test by checking that the backfill flags the 20 quiz runs above. Two of the six alert rules depend on these two detections, so both are silent today.
2. **No alert can reach anyone.** Every rule read back has `channelMask` email false, slack false, webhookCount 0 (files `20261011-write-config-results.json`, `...-more-alerts-results.json`). They show in the dashboard only. Action: add one email or webhook channel to at least "Critical safety stop".
3. **About 85% of the traces are one-span orphans, which makes the headline numbers misleading.** In two 10-minute samples (10 Oct 12:30 and 11 Oct 07:10) the traces that mention the K2 judge were 36 orphans to 6 story traces, and 82 orphans to 13 story traces. An orphan has an empty workflow name, the model name as its root span and 1 span lasting 2 to 11 s. 1,832 of the 2,095 traces mention K2. That is why p50 is 5.3 s while a story takes about 160 s, and why the 5.25% error rate and the 2,095 count do not describe stories. Cause not found: `src/storybound/oath/engine.py:189` and `pipeline.py:236,505,611` already copy `contextvars`, so the neatlogs span parent is probably not carried by that copy (hypothesis). Action: run one story and count root traces; fix the judge call so it joins the story trace; until then filter dashboards and alerts to workflow `create-storybook` with more than 10 spans. Smaller version of the same problem: standalone probe and eval calls are also traced alone (`84672c2c44e2` smoke test, `d705e66e2d99` K2 call, `1d57b0016612` judge-bias run); set `environment` (it is null on every trace) to `eval` or `test` for them in `src/storybound/tracing.py` or the app entry point.
4. **The 87 s Gemini stall (HR-005) is back and is the main latency cause.** HR-005 reverted to a 90 s timeout because the 42 later jobs showed no stall. On 11 Oct between 06:55 and 07:16 UTC 13 error traces had one `gemini-3.7-flash` call that ended at about 87 s with 504 "Deadline expired" (for example `6c8c28dda3c9`, `1092b1bbc158`, `d0bb16b76ed0`, `55bb3418fe6f`, `8e2a6a444965`). All shipped (retry worked). Stalls come in bursts: 9 traces on 10 Oct 07:58 to 09:47, 8 at 37 s during the 40 s experiment (12:22 to 12:28), 1 at 14:20, none from 12:49 to 14:19 except that one, then the 13 above. That pattern fits the provider being slow for some minutes, not our timeout. Action: reopen HR-005 and run the hedged retry its own text proposes (start a second call after about 15 s and take the first answer), measured on the 11 Oct burst.
5. **429 on text is fixed; 429 on pictures is not.** Since HR-007 (commit `3a89004`, 03:13 UTC on 11 Oct) 8 traces had a text 429 and all 8 shipped; before it 2 sweep-7 jobs ended in `error`. Pictures are different: 8 traces had image 429s with 6 to 48 failed spans each (`c9a78b746d47` 48 failed spans, 402 s; `aeea65c6b2cd` 31; `bcbaab155d9b` 32; `0fd459e70b51` 27), and `illustrate` failed 17 of 66 calls. The app falls back to text-only pages, so no child sees an error, but a story spends 3 to 5 minutes retrying (`node.media` 172 to 307 s). Action: after two image 429s in one story, stop painting for that story (the `auto` policy already stops after two failures; check it applies to the `full` and `half` policies too).
6. **Error spans without any error text (15 traces).** Gemini failures of 0.6 to 1.1 s (for example `182e4ea264be`, `9ac60464c282`, `33a9c06a4b76`, `57233238e74c`, `a32498d66523` all at 10 Oct 07:58 to 08:48 when three arms ran at once, and `21f5547097cb`, `2776b05792e0`, `83ec4cf94685` at 12:16 to 12:49) show ERROR but no message. Probably quota bursts, but unproven. Action: record exception type and message on every ERROR span in the model client wrapper.
7. **Three triage cards are still open** (`bdd1f6f1`, `ebcff17a`, `67e5d3bd`). Mark them resolved or archived in the dashboard with a link to `TRIAGE-REVIEW.md` (the CLI cannot write them). Evidence: `triage_open.json`.

## Watch

- **Parse errors persist.** 4 traces (`ac528975dda1` missing `image_prompt`; `e46e796a4a9e`, `06dac7f3455f` and `148a4920b0e0` "no JSON found" with the page text cut off at about 120 characters in the message). All but the first two on 10 Oct shipped after a retry; `148a4920b0e0` (11 Oct 06:58) and a second one, `e8a7ceeb2621`, still happened later, so the writer returns broken JSON in about 1 story in 20. Not seen by children. Check whether the writer output is cut (limit 900 tokens in `agents/writer.py:97,145`) before changing anything.
- **Image cost is invisible in neatlogs.** For text-only stories neatlogs measures 28% more than the ledger estimate (133 matched traces: estimate 2.03 USD, measured 2.61 USD, median ratio 0.79). For stories with pictures it sees 11 to 18% of the cost: `0fd459e70b51` $0.0411 measured against $0.358 estimated; `a7dd9ae1b832` $0.0382 against $0.356; `94db23729dac` $0.0344 against $0.191. The cfo.ai change (275839) is labelled text and verification, which is correct; do not quote a neatlogs figure as the cost of an illustrated story. Window total 4.59 USD is text only.
- **The `make-video` traces** (10 traces, 4 to 8 minutes, 3 of the 4 slowest). In `1cf9255c913b` (532 s) the child spans add up to about 170 s (`narrate_scenes` 169 s); the other 360 s sit in no child span (probably rendering; not verified). One failed: `49953358144a` (11 Oct 11:56 IST first preview, "five" not a number in the scene spec, 12 s; fixed since, later previews have no error).
- **Detections by day** (UTC; hourly files in `detection_trends.json`):

  Counts follow the number of runs per hour, so they do not show effect by themselves. Per story, from the ledger (B1 violations found per run): p1 8.5, then p2 (HR-001, commit 13:40 IST) 1.8, p3 (HR-003, 17:46 IST) 0.8, then rising to 1.6 to 3.1 as new promises and harder holdout drawings were added. Ungated B0: 7.3 then 3.5. HR-001 and HR-003 are visible in the per-story numbers; neatlogs hourly counts alone could not show them.

- **`ignore all` is still a critical term.** `06a2527e2d27` (benign christmas tree, 10 Oct 08:57) stopped on "ignore all" in a story. HR-004 kept steering phrases critical on purpose; check that a phrase like "ignore all the noise" is not flagged in a benign story.

  | `b8839d3c5c23`, `9226e2a194ba` | 10 Oct 07:49 | `evil-cat-knife-blood.png` refused (blood, weapon) in safety-eval and eval-2 | intended |

  | `06a2527e2d27` | 08:57 | "ignore all" in a benign christmas-tree story | false positive (still possible) |

  So 9 of 13 were false positives on benign text and 4 were intended. None of the 9 stopped a story (the ledger has no `stopped` outcome; the page was rewritten).
